This notebook writes `spack.yaml`. It should only answer:

> What scientific system dependencies does this project require?

Do not install the environment here.

```{python}
from rse_workbench.sci_sysdeps import default_spack_env, write_spack_yaml
```

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
DEFAULT_SYSTEM_SPECS = [
    "r@4.5.1 +X",
    "python@3.14",
    "libiconv",
    "ncurses",
    "openblas",
    "curl",
    "openssl",

dnf install -y git libicu-devel glpk-devel libxml2-devel cmake make libuv-devel libX11-devel libcurl-devel openssl-devel libgit2-devel fontconfig-devel freetype-devel cairo-devel libpng-devel libtiff-devel zlib-devel \
  fribidi-devel harfbuzz-devel libjpeg-turbo-devel libwebp-devel abseil-cpp-devel gdal-devel gdal geos-devel proj-devel sqlite-devel udunits2-devel
```

We can extend the default specs with Python:

```{python}
DEFAULT_SYSTEM_SPECS.extend([
    "glpk"
])
```

It can be useful to predict the system dependencies using
R's `pak::pkg_sysreqs()` function.


```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
spack_env = {
    "spack": {
        "specs": DEFAULT_SYSTEM_SPECS,
        "view": "/work/.spack-env/view",
        "packages": {
            "all": {
                "compiler": ["gcc@11.5.0"]
            }
        },
        "config": {
            "install_tree": {"root": "/work/.spack-env/install"},
            "source_cache": "/work/.spack/cache/source",
            "misc_cache": "/work/.spack/cache/misc",
            "build_stage": ["/work/.spack/stage"],
            "shared_linking": {
                "type": "rpath",
                "missing_library_policy": "error",
            },
        },
    }
}

write_spack_yaml(SPACK_YAML_PATH, spack_env)
SPACK_YAML_PATH
```
